content.intro: In this lesson, you will study migrating from bootstrap 4 to bootstrap 5 and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Migrating from Bootstrap 4 to Bootstrap 5 makes the interface more robust for real users and real content. Measure and reproduce behavior, inspect semantics and focus, and document the browser, viewport, steps, and result so another developer can repeat the check.

content_blocks.code: Migration checklist: inventory old markup/plugins → read the official v4-to-v5 guide → update data attributes and changed utilities → remove jQuery assumptions → test keyboard, responsive behavior, and all plugin states → stage rollout.
content_blocks.expected_output: The example illustrates migrating from bootstrap 4 to bootstrap 5. Expected review result: static-validation can be followed and the intended behavior or configuration can be explained; the lesson-specific acceptance checks still apply.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Read and apply the checklist, then record test evidence. This text example is not an executable program.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, undo one change at a time, and repeat the same browser/build check. Do not keep temporary debugging rules in the final implementation.

content_blocks.title: Version and implementation note
content_blocks.text: Legacy Bootstrap 4 migration is an optional maintenance task. Check the official migration guide for data attributes, removed jQuery dependency, renamed utilities, and form changes.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating migrating from bootstrap 4 to bootstrap 5 as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
